sentences.text: Houornis caudatus was a small bird featuring an elongated, toothy snout and perching feet.
It possessed an unusually long pygostyle, a structure made of fused tail vertebrae.
The animal is known only from fossil impressions rather than preserved bones.
The fossil was discovered in 1993 by Zhou Zhonghe near Boluochi in Liaoning Province, China.
The species was originally named Cathayornis caudatus in 1997 based on a mistaken belief that it had a long bony tail.
A specimen referred to the species in 1997 was confirmed as Houornis in 2015.
Houornis caudatus was previously classified as a species of Cathayornis and was once considered a nomen dubium.
Houornis lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
Some researchers consider Houornis dubious due to the poor preservation and incomplete nature of the fossil.
